title: Divine Vision and the Nature of Light
english: Having so much... it was going to be necessary and before the animals... in such a way it could not remain... not even... the 'was' signifies the ungenerated... God made the heaven and the earth (Genesis 1:1), whence the earth is not ungenerated. For not always 'was' signifies the eternal, but often... it happens in such a way that 'and there was a man of noble...' [gap]... invisible through the... constructed, since the things capable... came to this.

These things, indeed, [gap] he proposes to understand by word... we consider the invisible and unconstructed... by its own word, without and formless... of forms and shaped things... this is constructed from all... with its own matter and... in Wisdom it says: 'For the hand of your Almighty did not fail and create the cosmos out of formless matter...' [gap]... we only propose by word... 2. And darkness was upon the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters (Genesis 1:2). Darkness, indeed, someone might take as the sensible... having been light, it was darkness not existing... light subsisting, which was over the deep. The deep, however, is deep water, of which there is no measure to be taken, the depth being made manifest by length and breadth. He says the Spirit hovers over the water; and if the simplest understanding were to fall [gap]... lying upon the immeasurable water and especially... since the Spirit [gap] with the senses...

With such discourses, he sows spiritual things many times, he who even now performs the movement. Therefore, it is preserved, for they did not make [something] of waters according to nature, but [something else].

The abyss would be the darkness of ignorance. A holy [thing] is brought over the [powers], spirits, principalities, thrones, lordships. 'God saw the waters, and they saw and were afraid' (Job 38:16). It is evident, however, that it is not about sensible waters, for he neither fears nor sees, for they are inanimate; for God sees [not with eyes] but understands with unmixed and pure [intellect].

Evil exists in [things] according to nature, but virtue exists part by part from [knowledge]. 'And God said, Let there be light, and there was light' (Genesis 1:3). What light is [there] with the luminaries, as in 'Praise him, sun, and moon, praise him, all you stars and light' (Psalm 148:3)? They think another light exists from this, apart from the sun and the rest of the stars. Perhaps it is not entirely irreconcilable to have the notion that before the sun there was some radiance, thinking that another light was to be. For they say that [it] was not yet defining [something] for us, but [it] appeared. Some radiance leaps forward, an external radiance of the sun, the form of sensible lights, as if rays of light.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Divine Vision of Light
english: And of the heaven... [gaps] ...our [gaps] to be composed... [gaps] ...in them this is shown... [gaps] Just as on the earth... [gaps] ...plants later themselves... [gaps] ...a certain light previously existing... provided the generation of these [gaps] toward the allegory many [gaps] door, shepherd, way... [gaps] relation and philanthropy... [gaps] so also from the Father it is said to him: 'I have given you to be a light to the nations, to be salvation unto the ends of the earth' (Isa 49:6). This teaches not that he generated the Son out of non-being, but that, being light in essence, he set light to be for those dwelling with him from him.

For not when the light of this intelligible world was set, did it become light existing by itself; for 'was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world' (John 1:9). So also the Son, being wisdom eternally, becomes a teacher to be wise and to all as wisdom to those desiring to learn, not receiving wisdom as a beginning of being, but being eternally, for those of us being made wise; for she says about herself: 'Whenever he prepared the heavens, I was with him' (Prov 8:30), making it manifest to the Father: 'Wisdom, righteousness, and sanctification and redemption became ours' [gaps] ...opening [gaps] ...teaches the Psalmist... [gaps] ...God according to nature and... [gaps] ...himself divine... [gaps] ...creation... [gaps] so God is begotten... [gaps] according to allegory...

...following... the light that fits... because [we] shall be deprived... [we] received... at the same time as the generation... as [they] were foreknown... of their essence, which was enlightened by God... and to maintain the light unclouded... by the [will] of God. For he says, 'And God saw the light that [it was] good' (Genesis 1:4), that is, to take the naturally existing lights.

To see the light, it is necessary to hear in a manner befitting God, not concerning God through human passions or in human-like speech. For as 'he himself said and was born' [allusion to John 1:1], the one who spoke according to providence, so that we receive instead of saying his [word]... he wills... and concerning the... as previously stated... [it is] not equal to me... men indeed speak, but God [speaks through] the intellect... thus He speaks, not [with a] voice of God since [He is] not... but entering into... and the one hearing it... God [speaks] these things to the intellects; we say 'to say what God [said]'...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Demonstrating Divinity and the Distinction of Good and Evil
english: By the greatness of the light that has come, God would see the whole analogy and the harmony it has with other things. We say of the painter that he sees differently through art, even though he also receives it through sensory perception. For the one practicing art, seeing the analogy, perceives the beauty of this member in relation to that and this in relation to that, whereas the non-artist does not reach this appearance, which comes through calculation and technical intellect.

It has been said that the Savior is day; allegorically, 'the night has passed, and the day has approached' (Mark 1:5). For He Himself is day and light; light indeed according to essence, but [light] through intellect illuminates. For 'the sun of righteousness shall rise' (Malachi 4:2) 'upon you who fear my name.' Nor is it about a sensory light, but it rises as a sun to those who fear. And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night (Gen 1:5).

One must take all things according to the law of allegory. For the day is the shining of the law of allegory and illumination, and ignorance is darkness. The word 'called' signifies 'demonstrated'—for this is what is continually meant in the Scriptures. For 'made' sometimes also signifies 'demonstrated'; for the Jews say to the Savior, 'You, being a man, make yourself God' (John 10:34) instead of...

You demonstrate what you do by saying [missing] no one. And again it has been said that 'for this reason they sought to kill Jesus, not only because he broke the Sabbath, but because he also called God his own Father, making himself equal to God' (cf. John 10:30-33), which signifies equality with the unbegotten God. And John, in the epistle following him, writes: 'If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar' (1 John 1:8), making it clear that God [missing]—here is where the 'making' is the 'demonstrating' of the sign. But also concerning the priest who took [missing], it is said that 'the priest defiles him,' clearly meaning that the one 'defiling him' demonstrates that he has been defiled, not himself [missing] [missing].
